description: Animals whose whole cortex was removed did not fall into coma but became amnestic, kept coherent goal-directed behavior and showed excessive emotionality, and the rewarding effects of subcortical brain stimulation were preserved, in many species from the nineteenth century to modern studies.
limitations: The consciousness of the animals is inferred from behavior and from learned reward and punishment, within the problem of other minds.

sources.quote: Consciousness persists in the absence of cerebral cortex, as does volitional behavior.
